newsitem.title: HONG KONG: SHK Properties Ltd's Royal Ascot to boost interims.
newsitem.headline: SHK Properties Ltd's Royal Ascot to boost interims.

text.p: Sales of luxury flats at Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd's Royal Ascot residential development are expected to be the main driver behind interim earnings growth at the property developer, analysts said on Tuesday.

Sun Hung Kai Properties is due to release its results for the six months to December 31, 1996, on Thursday. It posted net profit of HK$5.15 billion (US$665 million) for the same period the previous year.
Michael Leary, senior property analyst at Lehman Brothers, said he forecast earnings per share of HK$2.32 compared with HK$2.22 for the six months to December 31, 1995.

"The most significant contributor in the first half is going to be Royal Ascot and the sale of units there. We are looking at pre-tax profit from that project alone of about HK$2.4 billion," Leary said.

"In terms of development, we are looking for about HK$3 billion to be booked in the first half of 1997 in pre-tax profit, and from a rental standpoint we are looking at around about HK$2 billion in operating profits," he said.
Carol Lai, research manager at SocGen-Crosby Securities, said Sun Hung Kai Properties had already secured 91 percent of its 1997 development profit to date.

She said sales at Sun Hung Kai's luxury residential King's Park Villa development in Ho Man Tin, in Kowloon, may also be included in the first-half results, bringing in HK$2.9 billion in pre-tax development profit.
She forecast interim net profit of about HK$7.6 billion.
"Fiscal year 1996 was a very bad year for Sun Hung Kai Properties so this is basically a rebound in its profits of which 69 percent will come from property disposal," said Lai.

She expected Phase II of the Royal Ascot development in Shatin in Hong Kong's New Territories to bring in HK$2.1 billion in pre-tax development profit and the Villa Tiara residential development in Tuen Mun, also in the New Territories, to contribute about HK$624 million.
"It is all a matter of assumption of booking of development profit," said Asia Equity research manager David Low.
"Royal Ascot is definitely coming through in the interims," he said, adding that the development would bring in profit of about HK$2.6 billion.
But he said the bulk of Sun Hung Kai Properties's projects would be completed in the second half of the year.

Low said King's Park rise would be a borderline case and if included in the first-half results could lead to a rise of 49 percent in interim earnings. "That is a very big scheme. We are talking about HK$2.7 billion in profit," said Low.

Sun Hung Kai Properties is also due to book an exceptional profit this fiscal year of about HK$500 million from the spinoff of SmarTone Telecommunications. Lai included the exceptional gain in her first-half forecast.
The mobile telephone operator listed shares in Hong Kong in October 1996. Before the listing, Sun Hung Kai Properties held a 40 percent stake in SmarTone.
"For the full year I am looking for 26.5 percent growth in bottom line, or about 23.1 percent taking out SmarTone," Lai added.
Leary said he expected fiscal 1997 earnings per share of HK$5.72 compared with HK$4.69 in fiscal 1996.
"We are very positive on the stock. The valuation is actually pretty attractive here," he said.
Sun Hung Kai Properties shares ended Tuesday unchanged at HK$84.25.
